subject: Clarify attribution for private/VPC latency exceptions — SentinelWorks go-live
messages:
From: Claire Burns <claire@sentinelworks.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: netops@sentinelworks.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA attribution for on-prem network events (SentinelWorks)

Hi Mateo,

We’re ramping toward a hard go-live for our private deployment with Redwood next month and we need to confirm how Redwood will treat latency/availability impacts that originate in our edge/router stack. Our operations team (cc’d) controls the WAN peering and the customer-managed border routers; we expect a small percentage of tail latency spikes during rolling config updates and occasional carrier jitter.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a carve-out or an "attribution appendix" that explicitly excludes customer-controlled network anomalies from the uptime SLA? If possible, we’d like the documentation to reference the types of evidence you require (e.g., traceroutes, router syslogs, BGP update windows) so our team can assemble that material in advance.

Attached is a short request summary and the go-live window (Aug 15) — we need an answer within two weeks to lock planning.

Thanks,
Claire Burns
Head of Platform Operations
SentinelWorks

Attachments: SLA_Exception_Request_SentinelWorks.pdf

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Claire Burns <claire@sentinelworks.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA attribution for on-prem network events (SentinelWorks)

Claire —

Thanks for the clear summary and the timeline. We can do an attribution appendix for Private/VPC customers where customer-controlled network elements are excluded from certain latency and availability calculations, but we need to lock down the exact scope and the evidence chain. High level:

- What we can exclude: latency spikes or outages with demonstrated origin in customer-managed border devices or WAN carrier handoffs, where Redwood infrastructure (control plane + serving runtime) shows normal health.
- What we need from you: time-correlated traceroutes, router syslogs, BGP update snippets, and a short post-event packet-capture sample where available. We require at least two data points demonstrating the same class of event for recurring patterns; single transient carrier blips may be handled case-by-case.

I’m attaching a draft of a "shared-responsibility appendix" that maps attribution categories and the minimal evidence list. Karthik — could you review the network/latency wording and suggest any technical clarifications? Vanessa — I’ve copied you to keep CS in the loop for the go-live sequence and runbook.

Proposed next steps:
1) Karthik to provide a technical addendum for latency attribution (by EOD tomorrow).
2) We finalize appendix and legal will fold it into the PO/contract (target by Aug 8).
3) Sentinel sends sample evidence templates and the final network diagram.

If this plan works, I’ll flag it to Legal and Solutions so we can expedite.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0198

Attachment: redwood-shared-resp-proposal.docx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, Claire Burns <claire@sentinelworks.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2028 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA attribution for on-prem network events (SentinelWorks)

Claire / Mateo —

Quick technical note to make the appendix concrete so Legal can sign off:

1) Attribution criteria (examples):
   - Customer-controlled: packet loss/latency observed only at customer egress/ingress IPs, confirmed by traceroute with hop loss consistent at the first/second hop and not present in Redwood edge telemetry.
   - Carrier/Transit: BGP flap or upstream carrier degradation that shows correlated jumps across multiple customer prefixes (we will ask for carrier incident id if available).
   - Redwood fault: increased latency or error rates accompanied by runtime stack traces, KV cache pressure, or GPU node health alerts.

2) Evidence format: time-windowed CSV of traceroute hops (timestamped), a 10–30s tcpdump excerpt for sample events (pcap summary preferred), and router syslog extracts with timestamps in ISO8601. All evidence should include at least one synchronized timestamp source (NTP/chrony) noted in the header.

3) SLA math: For uptime/latency SLOs we will exclude minutes flagged under "customer-attributed network incidents" from the denominator when calculating rolling 30-day latency percentiles, but not from per-request billing metrics. Exception: if Redwood serving runtime shows degraded health during that window, the incident remains candidate for Redwood attribution.

I’ve also sketched an automated evidence intake checklist that can be submitted to us (we’ll drop into the support runbook).

On a pragmatic note: given your Aug 15 go-live, we should get the network diagram and one sample traceroute by Aug 3 to give Legal time.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, this is helpful and aligns with our internal expectations. We’ll assemble the network diagram (sentinel-net-diagram-v2.pdf) and a representative traceroute + syslog extract and upload to the Drive link you provided by COB Aug 3.

- Is there a simple template you prefer for the traceroute / pcap summary so we don’t miss fields?

We’d also appreciate an accelerated review from Legal — we’ll need the appendix in the PO before we finalize the carrier change on Aug 12. If you can flag this as an expedited exception (HS-45321), that helps our procurement team.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Claire Burns

SentinelWorks
